cleanIntro: The SW22 Victory comes apart on a single takedown screw: barrel and receiver lift off the grip frame as one assembly and the bolt then slides out the back. Deep Clean covers barrel removal, which the manual says is not needed for regular cleaning, and the magazine.

steps.title: Standard Victory or Performance Center?
steps.action: Establish which SW22 Victory you have before you start. The standard model's trigger overtravel screw is factory set and needs no adjustment from you; some Performance Center models add adjustable trigger takeup and overtravel, and some carry a muzzle compensator. The model name and serial number are marked on the receiver — note the serial number, because Smith & Wesson asks owners to record it before shipping a firearm in for service.
steps.prose: It changes what your cleaning session has to include rather than how the pistol comes apart. A compensator has to have its bore channel cleaned of lead and carbon every time regardless of ammunition brand, and a Performance Center trigger has screws that a careless bench session can move. The takedown itself is identical on both.
steps.quote: The trigger overtravel screw on the standard model is factory set and does not require any further adjustment by the user. Some Performance Center® models include the ability to adjust trigger takeup/pretravel and overtravel.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Model and Features Identification / Trigger Adjustment Screw(s), p.11

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt back, bolt stop up
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and the trigger fully forward, press the magazine release and take the magazine out. Then grasp the serrated sides of the bolt from the rear, draw it briskly fully rearward to clear the chamber, and lock it open by pressing the bolt stop lever up.
steps.prose: This pistol has a bolt running inside a fixed receiver rather than a slide over a barrel, so what you grip is the small serrated ear at the rear — there is no slide to take hold of. Draw it briskly and fully: .22 LR is short and light, and a slow pull will drag a live round out of the chamber and let it fall back into the action instead of throwing it clear.
steps.quote: Lock the bolt into the open position by pressing the bolt stop lever to the up position (FIGURE 26).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.23

steps.title: Look into the chamber
steps.action: With the bolt held open, look into the chamber and make certain it is clear. Then close the bolt on the empty chamber before you go on.
steps.prose: The bolt has to be closed for the strip, which is unusual — most pistols come apart with the action locked open — so this is the last look you get. A .22 rimfire case that failed to eject can lie in the receiver where it is easy to miss, and it will be trapped under the bolt the moment you close it.
steps.quote: Make certain that the chamber is clear (FIGURE 27).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.23

steps.title: 1/8 inch hex wrench, takedown screw counter-clockwise
steps.action: Using the 1/8 inch hex wrench supplied with the pistol, loosen the takedown screw by turning it counter-clockwise. This may require significant pressure.
steps.prose: The screw is torqued and it is the only fastener holding the gun together, so expect it to resist — the manual says so explicitly. Use the supplied wrench fully seated in the socket; a slightly small hex key or a worn one will round the socket out, and there is no other way to open this pistol.
steps.quote: Using the 1/8˝ hex wrench provided, loosen the takedown screw (FIGURE 28) by turning it counter-clockwise. This may require significant pressure.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Hold barrel and frame together while the screw comes out
steps.action: Keep one hand holding the barrel and frame together as you take the takedown screw all the way out.
steps.prose: Once that screw is clear there is nothing but the rear tabs holding the two halves of the pistol in register, and a Victory that is allowed to fall open drops the bolt straight out of the back of the receiver. One hand on the assembly, one on the wrench.
steps.quote: While holding the barrel and frame together with one hand, remove the takedown screw completely.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Muzzle up a quarter inch, then barrel and receiver forward off the frame
steps.action: Tip the muzzle end up about a quarter of an inch, then pull the barrel and receiver assembly forward, off the tabs at the rear that hold the two together, and away from the grip frame.
steps.prose: The tip-up is what disengages the rear tabs — try to lift the assembly straight off and it stays hooked. It is a small movement, about a quarter inch at the muzzle, and levering harder instead of tipping is what bends the tabs. As soon as the assembly is clear of the frame the bolt is free to slide out of the back of the receiver, so keep the muzzle up.
steps.caution: Once lifted clear of the frame, the bolt is free to slide out the rear of the receiver. Take care not to drop the bolt.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel/receiver assembly from the frame by tipping the muzzle end up slightly (FIGURE 29) and pulling the assembly forward, off the tabs at the rear that hold them together and away from the grip frame (FIGURE 30).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Withdraw the bolt from the rear of the receiver
steps.action: Grasp the bolt at its serrated area and withdraw it rearward out of the receiver. Set it down carefully — the recoil spring is compressed inside it.
steps.prose: Do not squeeze or lever the bolt anywhere except the serrations. The recoil spring lives inside the bolt on this pistol and is held only by the guide rod head sitting in a cutout, so a thumb pressing in the wrong place while you clean can pop the assembly out. The manual is explicit that the spring and guide rod do not need to come out for normal cleaning.
steps.quote: Grasp the bolt at the serrated area and withdraw it from the receiver (FIGURE 31).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.24
steps.warn: The recoil spring is compressed within the bolt and will fly out with considerable force if not controlled. It is not required that the recoil spring and guide rod be removed for normal cleaning.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel and receiver, bolt, grip frame, takedown screw and magazine — that is the SW22 Victory field stripped for cleaning. Clean the bolt without dislodging the guide rod, and do not dry fire the pistol with the barrel and receiver off the frame. Deep Clean covers barrel removal and the magazine, both of which the manual documents separately.
steps.prose: Barrel removal is optional by the manual's own account rather than part of a normal clean, which is why it sits on the deep path rather than here.
steps.quote: DO NOT DRY FIRE YOUR PISTOL WHEN THE BARREL / RECEIVER IS OFF THE FRAME, AS DAMAGE TO THE PISTOL MAY RESULT.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, WARNING, p.25

deepSteps.title: Guide rod and recoil spring out of the bolt
deepSteps.action: If the bolt genuinely needs stripping, note first that the recoil spring is held in place by the guide rod, which is itself held by a cutout in the bolt. Compress the spring slightly and lift the assembly up and out of its notch from the bottom of the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: This is optional work and the manual says so — the spring and guide rod are not required to come out for normal cleaning. If you do it, keep the spring compressed the whole time and lift out of the notch rather than pulling along the bolt; letting go partway is what sends it across the room. It goes back with the large end of the guide rod to the rear.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the guide rod and recoil spring, compress the spring slightly and lift the assembly up and out of its notch from the bottom of the bolt (FIGURE 35).
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.25
deepSteps.warn: The recoil spring is compressed within the bolt and will fly out with considerable force if not controlled.

deepSteps.title: Barrel set screw loosened — several turns, not out
deepSteps.action: With the pistol already field stripped, loosen the barrel set screw at the bottom front of the receiver with the supplied hex wrench. Several turns counter-clockwise is enough; you do not need to remove the screw completely.
deepSteps.prose: Removal of the barrel is not necessary for regular cleaning and maintenance — this is a job for a genuinely fouled or a swapped barrel. The set screw drops into a detent in the barrel rather than clamping it, so backing it out a few turns is all that is needed; taking it right out only risks losing it.
deepSteps.quote: Loosen the barrel set screw at the bottom front of the receiver with the hex wrench provided (FIGURE 38a). Several turns counterclockwise should suffice. You do not need to completely remove the screw.
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Barrel Removal, p.26

deepSteps.title: Pull barrel and receiver straight apart
deepSteps.action: Grasp the barrel in one hand and the receiver in the other and pull them apart. Some effort may be needed if the parts are dirty.
deepSteps.prose: The parts are a slip fit — no turning is required and none is possible, so twisting to free a tight barrel only galls the mating surfaces. If it will not part, the set screw has not been backed off far enough or fouling is the reason, and both are solved without force. The barrel is shaped so it will only re-enter the receiver in the correct orientation.
deepSteps.quote: The parts are a slip fit - no turning is required or possible.
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Barrel Removal, p.26

deepSteps.title: Magazine: screwdriver through the slot, spring compressed an inch
deepSteps.action: With the magazine out and empty, insert a small screwdriver shaft through the slot in the magazine tube and through the spring, then compress the spring about an inch to take the tension off the butt plate. With the spring held away from it, slide the butt plate off the tube.
deepSteps.prose: The screwdriver shaft becomes the thing holding the spring, which is what makes this safe — pull the butt plate without it and the spring exits at speed. An inch of compression is enough to clear the plate; more than that just makes the shaft harder to hold.
deepSteps.quote: Compress the spring in the magazine approximately one inch to relieve the tension on the magazine butt plate.
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Magazine Disassembly, p.29
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the spring and follower so that they do not fly out and cause injury.

deepSteps.title: Spring out, then the load assist button and follower
deepSteps.action: Control the spring as you release the tension and withdraw the screwdriver, then take the spring out of the tube. Slide the magazine load assist button down to the hole at the bottom of the tube and pull it out of the follower and tube, then remove the follower.
deepSteps.prose: The load assist button — the thumb tab on the side of a .22 magazine — is what pins the follower, and it only comes out at that one wider hole near the bottom. Sliding it there first is the whole trick; trying to prise it out anywhere else breaks the tab. Clean inside the tube while it is open, because rimfire residue in a .22 magazine is the usual cause of a follower that hangs.
deepSteps.quote: Slide the magazine load assist button down to the hole at the bottom of the magazine tube and pull it out of the follower and tube (FIGURE 48).
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW22 VICTORY® Pistol — REV:SW22_VICTORY_080118 — Magazine Disassembly, p.30

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish with a dry cotton cloth patch to carry out residue and solvent
Clean the chamber mouth and feed ramp — rimfire wax and lead build here faster than anywhere else
If the pistol has the Performance Center compensator, clean its bore channel of lead and carbon every time

cleaning.name: BOLT AND RECEIVER
tasks: Clean the bolt face, the extractor and the firing pin recess
Clean the bolt raceways inside the receiver and the ejector
Be careful not to unintentionally dislodge the recoil spring and guide rod while cleaning the bolt
Clean the takedown screw and its threaded hole

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the tube, the feed lips and the load assist button slot
If the magazine has been apart, clean inside the tube and the follower before reassembly
Check the butt plate is secure by trying to remove it partially — the spring is under tension and will fly out if the cover comes off quickly

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: One drop of firearm lubricant on top of the bolt
One drop on each rail along both sides of the bolt
One drop on the side of the extractor with the bolt open
Do not over-lubricate: excess collects unburned powder and carbon residue and interferes with proper functioning

reassembly: If the barrel was removed, insert it fully into the receiver — it is shaped to enter only in the correct orientation — then tighten the barrel set screw until it is snug, and check its tightness periodically thereafter.
If the bolt was stripped, reassemble the spring on the guide rod with the large end of the guide rod to the rear and compress it until the head of the guide rod returns to its cutout in the bolt.
Slide the bolt into the rear of the receiver, then set the barrel and receiver assembly onto the grip frame, engaging the rear tabs and lowering the muzzle end into place.
Replace the takedown screw and tighten it snug with the supplied wrench so there is no gap at the joint, and check its tightness periodically.

Magazine: install the follower lining up its bottom hole with the key hole, insert the load assist button into the follower from the left side, replace the spring, then compress it about an inch with a screwdriver shaft and slide the butt plate fully on.
fncheck: Before loading, check that the takedown screw and the barrel set screw are both snug and that there is no gap where the receiver meets the frame. Hand-cycle the bolt several times pointed in a safe direction and confirm it runs fully forward into battery, that the bolt stop holds it open and releases cleanly, and that the extractor snaps back. Then seat an empty magazine, confirm it latches and drops free, and check the trigger and controls operate normally before the pistol goes back into use.
